newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks close lower after quiet JR West debut.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks close lower after quiet JR West debut.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed lower in subdued trading on Tuesday, with investors' attention on the lacklustre debut of West Japan Railway Co. Brokers said sluggishness would linger until Japan's political climate becomes clear after general elections on October 20.
The key 225-share Nikkei average was down 122.48 points or 0.58 percent to close at 21,038.53. Its December futures shed 170 points to 21,030.
"The Nikkei average is not likely to break out of the current range for the time being," said Tetsuya Ishijima, chief strategist at Okasan Securities Co Ltd.
Shares in West Japan Railway Co (JR West) had a first traded price of 360,000 yen on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, below the 370,000 to 430,000 yen that many analysts had expected.
Brokers said the low price reflected gloomy sentiment in the Tokyo market recently amid an unclear political outlook.
"The JR West listing turned out to be a case of unexpectedly bad timing," said Akishige Ishikura, an analyst at Dai-Ichi Securities Co Ltd.
But brokers also said the price was a relief as it was likely to help stabilise trading, unlike the overheated listings of other state-owned firms in the past.
The JR West shares closed at 367,000 yen on Tuesday.

"Individual investors are happy as long as the shares trade above the public offer price of 357,000 yen," said Okasan's Ishijima. But he added that heavy selling orders were placed above 370,000 yen, indicating that the share price might be capped for the time being.
The Dow industrial's rally to an intra-day high above 6,000 overnight failed to inspire buying momentum in Tokyo.
The Nikkei average briefly slipped below a 21,000 support line, for the first time since September 17, and later managed to claw back above that level.
Brokers said the key index was likely to be trapped between 20,500 and 21,500 at least until the general elections on October 20.
"The election campaign was launched today, but the framework of a new government is still unclear," Ishijima said.
Turnover remained light at about 235 million shares on Tuesday, against 199 million shares on Wednesday.
In other indices, the TOPIX index of all first section stocks fell 9.16 points or 0.58 percent to end at 1,581.72.
The Nikkei 300 average was down 1.73 points or 0.58 percent at 296.01.
Declining issues outnumbered advancers 750 to 272, while 208 issues were unchanged.
Losing sectors were led by automobiles, railway/bus, air transport, iron/steel and rubber.
The only major gainers were warehousing and pulp/paper.
The second section index was down 6.39 points or 0.31 percent to close at 2,078.60, with 7.80 million shares traded.
The over-the-counter (OTC) index fished down 4.78 points or 0.31 percent at 1,543.07.
-- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk (81-3-3432-8027)
